passage.title: THE NEIGHBOURHOOD LIBRARY
passage.subtitle: More than just a quiet room of books
paragraphs: Five years ago, Elmwood Library nearly closed because the town did not have enough money to keep it open. However, twenty local people decided to volunteer their time to save the building and turn it into a lively community hub.

Today, the library is open six days a week from Tuesday to Sunday. Visitors can still borrow novels, history books, travel guides and magazines for free. There are also six public computers with free internet access for anyone who needs to write a CV or do homework.

Besides books, the library hosts a busy calendar of weekly events. On Wednesday afternoons, retired teachers help primary school pupils with their reading. On Friday mornings, older neighbours meet in the café corner for free tea and a friendly chess game.
Mrs Evans, who has managed the volunteers since 2021, says the library brings young and old people together. She is proud that more than four hundred families now hold active library cards.
